questions.question: The internal audit department wrote some scripts that are used for continuous auditing. The IT department asked for copies of the scripts so that they can be used for setting up a continuous monitoring process on key systems. Considering the ability of the information systems (IS) auditors to independently and objectively audit the IT function, should sharing these scripts be permitted?

options.A: Sharing the scripts is not permitted because it gives IT the ability to pre-audit systems and avoid an accurate, comprehensive audit.
options.B: Sharing the scripts is required because IT must have the ability to review all programs and software that run on information systems regardless of audit independence.
options.C: Sharing the scripts is permissible if IT recognizes that audits may be conducted in areas not covered in the scripts.
options.D: Sharing the scripts is not permitted because the IS auditors who wrote the scripts would not be permitted to audit any information systems where the scripts are being used for monitoring.

questions.correct_explanation: IS audit may not be able to review the effectiveness of the scripts, but it can still audit all aspects of the systems.

wrong_explanations.A: The ability of IT to continuously monitor and address any issues on IT systems does not affect the ability of information systems (IS) audit to perform a comprehensive audit.
wrong_explanations.B: Sharing the scripts may be required by policy for quality assurance and configuration management, but that does not impair the ability to audit.
wrong_explanations.D: An audit of an IS system encompasses more than just the controls covered in the scripts.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST factor for determining the required extent of data collection during the planning phase of an information systems (IS) compliance audit?

options.A: Complexity of the organization's operation
options.B: Findings and issues noted from the prior year
options.C: Purpose, objective and scope of the audit
options.D: Auditor's familiarity with the organization

questions.correct_explanation: The extent to which data will be collected during an information systems (IS) audit is related directly to the purpose, objective and scope of the audit. An audit with a narrow purpose and limited objective and scope is most likely to result in less data collection than an audit with a wider purpose and scope. Statistical analysis may also determine the extent of data collection, such as sample size or means of data collection,

wrong_explanations.A: The complexity of the organization's operation is a factor in the planning of an audit but does not directly affect the determination of how much data to collect. The extent of data collection is subject to the intensity, scope and purpose of the audit.
wrong_explanations.B: Prior findings and issues are factors in the planning of an audit but do not directly affect the determination of how much data to collect. Data must be collected outside of areas of previous findings.
wrong_explanations.D: An auditor's familiarity with the organization is a factor in the planning of an audit but does not directly affect the determination of how much data to collect. The audit must be based on sufficient evidence of the monitoring of controls and not unduly influenced by the auditor's familiarity with the organization.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is developing an audit plan for an environment that includes new systems. Enterprise management wants the IS auditor to focus on recently implemented systems. How should the IS auditor respond?

options.A: Audit the new systems as requested by management.
options.B: Audit systems not included in last year's scope.
options.C: Determine the highest-risk systems and plan accordingly.
options.D: Audit systems not in last year's scope and the new systems.

questions.correct_explanation: The best action is to conduct a risk assessment and design the audit plan to cover the areas of highest risk. ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Standard 1201 (Risk Assessment in Planning), statement 1201.1: "The IT audit and assurance function shall use an appropriate risk assessment approach (i.e., data-driven with both quantitative and qualitative factors) and supporting methodology to develop the overall IT audit plan and to determine priorities for the effective allocation of IT audit resources."
questions.framework_ref: ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Standard 1201

wrong_explanations.A: Auditing the new systems does not reflect a risk-based approach. Although the systems can contain sensitive data and may present risk of data loss or disclosure to the organization, without a risk assessment, the decision to solely audit the newly implemented systems is not a risk-based decision.
wrong_explanations.B: Auditing systems not included in the previous year's scope does not reflect a risk-based approach. In addition, management may know about problems with the new systems and may intentionally try to steer the audit away from that vulnerable area. Although, at first, the new system may seem to be the riskiest area, an assessment must be conducted rather than relying on the judgment of the information systems (IS) auditor or IT manager.
wrong_explanations.D: The creation of the audit plan should be performed in cooperation with management and based on risk. The IS auditor should not arbitrarily decide on what needs to be audited.

tips: Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: What BEST describes the risk that information collected may contain a material error that may go undetected during information systems (IS) auditing?

options.A: Inherent risk
options.B: Audit risk
options.C: Control risk
options.D: Detection risk

questions.correct_explanation: Audit risk is the probability that information or financial reports may contain material errors and that the auditor may not detect an error that has occurred.

wrong_explanations.A: Inherent risk is the risk level or exposure of the process/entity to be audited without considering the controls that management has implemented.
wrong_explanations.C: Control risk is the risk that a material error exists that would not be prevented or detected on a timely basis by the system of internal controls.
wrong_explanations.D: Detection risk is the risk that material errors or misstatements that have occurred will not be detected by an information systems (IS) auditor.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: For which of the following controls would an information systems (IS) auditor look in an environment where duties cannot be appropriately segregated?

options.A: Overlapping controls
options.B: Boundary controls
options.C: Access controls
options.D: Compensating controls

questions.correct_explanation: Compensating controls are internal controls that are intended to reduce the risk of an existing or potential control weakness that may arise when duties cannot be appropriately segregated.

wrong_explanations.A: Overlapping controls are two controls addressing the same control objective or exposure. Because primary controls cannot be achieved when duties cannot or are not appropriately segregated, it is difficult to install overlapping controls.
wrong_explanations.B: Boundary controls establish the interface between the would-be user of a computer system and the computer system itself and are individual-based, not role-based, controls.
wrong_explanations.C: Access controls for resources are based on individuals and not on roles. For a lack of separation of duties, the information systems (IS) auditor expects to find that a person has higher levels of access than are ideal. The IS auditor wants to find compensating controls to address this risk.

tips: Watch for separation-of-duties violations: the same actor authorizing AND executing, designing AND testing, or developing AND deploying.

questions.question: Which of the following is a KEY benefit of a control self-assessment (CSA)?

options.A: Management ownership of the internal controls supporting business objectives is reinforced.
options.B: Audit expenses are reduced when the assessment results are an input to external audit work.
options.C: Fraud detection is improved because internal business staff are engaged in testing controls.
options.D: Internal auditors can shift to a consultative approach by using the results of the assessment.

questions.correct_explanation: The objective of control self-assessment (CSA) is to have business management become more aware of the importance of internal control and their responsibility in terms of corporate governance.

wrong_explanations.B: Reducing audit expenses is not a key benefit of CSA.
wrong_explanations.C: Improved fraud detection is important but not as important as control ownership. It is not a principal objective of CSA.
wrong_explanations.D: CSA may give more insights to internal auditors, allowing them to take a more consultative role; however, this is an additional benefit, not the key benefit.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY requirement that a data mining and auditing software tool should meet? The software tool should:

options.A: interface with various types of enterprise resource planning software and databases.
options.B: accurately capture data from the enterprise systems without causing excessive performance problems.
options.C: introduce audit hooks into the financial systems of the enterprise to support continuous auditing.
options.D: be customizable and support inclusion of custom programming to aid in investigative analysis.

questions.correct_explanation: Although all the requirements that are listed as answer choices are desirable in a software tool evaluated for auditing and data mining purposes, the most critical requirement is that the tool works effectively on the systems of the enterprise being audited.

wrong_explanations.A: The product must interface with the types of systems used by the enterprise and provide meaningful data for analysis.
wrong_explanations.C: The tool should probably work on more than just financial systems and does not necessarily require implementation of audit hooks.
wrong_explanations.D: The tool should be flexible but not necessarily customizable. It should have built-in analysis software tools.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: A long-term IT employee with a strong technical background and broad managerial experience has applied for a vacant position in the information systems (IS) audit department. Determining whether to hire this individual for this position should be PRIMARILY based on the individual's experience and:

options.A: length of service because this will help ensure technical competence.
options.B: age because training in audit techniques may be impractical.
options.C: IT knowledge because this will bring enhanced credibility to the audit function.
options.D: ability, as an IS auditor, to be independent of existing IT relationships.

questions.correct_explanation: Independence should be continually assessed by the auditor and management. This assessment should consider such factors as changes in personal relationships, financial interests, and prior job assignments and responsibilities.

wrong_explanations.A: Length of service does not ensure technical competency.
wrong_explanations.B: Evaluating an individual's qualifications based on the age of the individual is not a good criterion and is illegal in many parts of the world.
wrong_explanations.C: The fact that the employee has worked in IT for many years may not ensure credibility. The information systems (IS) audit department's needs should be defined, and any candidate should be evaluated against those requirements.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: For a retail business with a large volume of transactions, which of the following audit techniques is the MOST appropriate for addressing emerging risk?

options.A: Use of computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs)
options.B: Quarterly risk assessments
options.C: Sampling of transaction logs
options.D: Continuous auditing

questions.correct_explanation: The implementation of continuous auditing enables a real-time feed of information to management through automated reporting processes so that management may implement corrective actions more quickly.

wrong_explanations.A: Using software tools such as computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs) to analyze transaction data can provide detailed analysis of trends and potential risk, but it is not as effective as continuous auditing, because a time differential may exist between executing the software and analyzing the results.
wrong_explanations.B: Quarterly risk assessment may be a good technique but not as responsive as continuous auditing.
wrong_explanations.C: The sampling of transaction logs is a valid audit technique; however, risk may exist that is not captured in the transaction log, and the analysis may have a potential time lag.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing access to an application to determine whether recently added accounts were appropriately authorized. This is an example of:

options.A: variable sampling.
options.B: substantive testing.
options.C: compliance testing.
options.D: stop-or-go sampling.

questions.correct_explanation: Compliance testing determines whether controls are being applied in compliance with policy. This includes tests to determine whether new accounts were appropriately authorized.

wrong_explanations.A: Variable sampling is used to estimate numerical values, such as dollar values.
wrong_explanations.B: Substantive testing substantiates the integrity of actual processing, such as balances on financial statements. The development of substantive tests is often dependent on the outcome of compliance tests. If compliance tests indicate that internal controls are adequate, then substantive tests can be minimized.
wrong_explanations.D: Stop-or-go sampling allows a test to be stopped as early as possible and is not appropriate for checking whether procedures have been followed.

tips: Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: The decisions and actions of an information systems (IS) auditor are MOST likely to affect which of the following types of risk?

options.A: Inherent
options.B: Detection
options.C: Control
options.D: Business

questions.correct_explanation: Detection risk is directly affected by the IS auditor's selection of audit procedures and techniques. Detection risk is the risk that a review will not detect or notice a material issue.

wrong_explanations.A: Inherent risk is the risk that a material error could occur, if there are no related internal controls to prevent or detect the error. Inherent risk is not usually affected by an information systems (IS) auditor.
wrong_explanations.C: Control risk is the risk that a material error exists that would not be prevented or detected on a timely basis by the system of internal controls. Control risk can be mitigated by the actions of enterprise management.
wrong_explanations.D: Business risk is a probable situation with uncertain frequency and magnitude of loss (or gain). Business risk is usually not directly affected by an IS auditor.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST critical step when planning an information systems (IS) audit?

options.A: Review findings from prior audits.
options.B: Obtain executive management approval of the audit plan
options.C: Review information security policies and procedures.
options.D: Perform a risk assessment.

questions.correct_explanation: Of all the steps listed, performing a risk assessment is the most critical. Risk assessment is required by ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Standard 1201 (Risk Assessment in Planning), statement 1201.2: "IT audit and assurance practitioners shall identify and assess risk relevant to the area under review when planning individual engagements." In addition to the standards requirement, if a risk assessment is not performed, then high-risk areas of the auditee systems or operations may not be identified for evaluation.
questions.framework_ref: ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Standard 1201

wrong_explanations.A: The findings of a previous audit are of interest to the auditor, but they are not the most critical step. The most critical step involves finding the current issues or high-risk areas, not reviewing the resolution of older issues. A review of historical audit findings can indicate that management is not resolving the items or the recommendation was ineffective.
wrong_explanations.B: Executive management is not required to approve the audit plan. It is typically approved by the audit committee or board of directors. Management can recommend areas to audit.
wrong_explanations.C: Reviewing information security policies and procedures is normally conducted during fieldwork, not planning.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing a software application that is built on the principles of service-oriented architecture. What is the INITIAL step?

options.A: Understanding services and their allocation to business processes by reviewing the service repository documentation
options.B: Sampling the use of service security standards as represented by the Security Assertions Markup Language (SAML)
options.C: Reviewing the service level agreements established for all system providers
options.D: Auditing the core service and its dependencies on other systems

questions.correct_explanation: A service-oriented architecture relies on the principles of a distributed environment in which services encapsulate business logic as a black box and might be deliberately combined to depict real-world business processes. Before reviewing services in detail, it is essential for the information systems (IS) auditor to comprehend the mapping of business processes to services.

wrong_explanations.B: Sampling the use of service security standards as represented by Security Assertions Markup Language (SAML) is an essential follow-up step to understanding services and their allocation to business but is not the initial step.
wrong_explanations.C: Reviewing the service level agreements is an essential follow-up step to understanding services and their allocation to business but is not the initial step.
wrong_explanations.D: Auditing the core service and its dependencies with others is most likely a part of the audit, but the IS auditor must first gain an understanding of the business processes and how the systems support those processes.

tips: Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor conducting a review of software usage and licensing discovers that numerous PCs contain unauthorized software. Which of the following actions should the IS auditor take?

options.A: Delete all copies of the unauthorized software.
options.B: Recommend an automated process to monitor for compliance with software licensing.
options.C: Report the use of the unauthorized software and the need to prevent recurrence.
options.D: Warn the end users about the risk of using illegal software.

questions.correct_explanation: The use of unauthorized or illegal software should be prohibited by an organization. An IS auditor must convince the user and management of the risk and the need to eliminate the risk. For example, software piracy can result in exposure and severe fines.

wrong_explanations.A: An information systems (IS) auditor should not assume the role of the enforcing officer and take on any personal involvement in removing the unauthorized software.
wrong_explanations.B: This would detect compliance with software licensing; however, an automated solution might not be the best option in all cases.
wrong_explanations.D: Auditors must report material findings to management for action. Informing the users of risk is not the primary responsibility of the IS auditor.,

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An audit charter should:

options.A: be dynamic and change to coincide with the changing nature of technology and the audit profession.
options.B: clearly state the audit objectives and delegation of authority for the maintenance and review of internal controls.
options.C: document the audit procedures designed to achieve the planned audit objectives.
options.D: outline the overall authority, scope and responsibilities of the audit function.

questions.correct_explanation: An audit charter should state management objectives for, and delegation of authority to, information systems (IS) auditors.

wrong_explanations.A: The audit charter should not be subject to changes in technology and should not significantly change over time. The charter should be approved at the highest level of management.
wrong_explanations.B: An audit charter states the authority and reporting requirements for the audit but not the details of maintenance of internal controls.
wrong_explanations.C: An audit charter is not at a detailed level and, therefore, does not include specific audit objectives or procedures.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor finds a small number of user access requests that were not authorized by managers through the normal predefined workflow steps and escalation rules. The IS auditor should:

options.A: perform an additional analysis.
options.B: report the problem to the audit committee.
options.C: conduct a security risk assessment.
options.D: recommend that the owner of the identity management system fix the workflow issues.

questions.correct_explanation: The information systems (IS) auditor needs to perform substantive testing and additional analysis to determine why the approval and workflow processes are not working as intended. Before making any recommendation, the IS auditor should gain a good understanding of the scope of the problem and the factors that caused this incident. The IS auditor should identify whether the issue was caused by managers not following procedures, a problem with the workflow of the automated system or a combination of the two.

wrong_explanations.B: The IS auditor does not yet have enough information to report the problem.
wrong_explanations.C: Changing the scope of the IS audit or conducting a security risk assessment requires more detailed information about the processes and violations being reviewed.
wrong_explanations.D: The IS auditor must first determine the root cause and impact of the findings and does not have enough information to recommend fixing the workflow issues.

tips: When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: Which of the following sampling methods is MOST useful when testing for compliance?

options.A: Attribute sampling
options.B: Variable sampling
options.C: Stratified mean-per-unit sampling
options.D: Difference estimation sampling

questions.correct_explanation: Attribute sampling is the primary sampling method used for compliance testing. Attribute sampling is a sampling model that is used to estimate the rate of occurrence of a specific quality (attribute) in a population and is used in compliance testing to confirm whether the quality exists. For example, an attribute sample may check all transactions over a certain predefined dollar amount for proper approvals.

wrong_explanations.B: Variable sampling is based on the calculation of a mean from a sample extracted from the entire population and using that to estimate the characteristics of the entire population. For example, a sample of 10 items shows an average price of US $10 per item. For the entire population of 1,000 items, the total value is estimated to be US $10,000. This is not a good way to measure compliance with a process.
wrong_explanations.C: Stratified mean-per-unit sampling attempts to ensure that the entire population is represented in the sample. This is not an effective way to measure compliance.
wrong_explanations.D: Difference estimation sampling examines measure deviations and extraordinary items and is not a good way to measure compliance.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: When testing program change requests for a remote system, an information systems (IS) auditor finds that the number of changes available for sampling does not provide a reasonable level of assurance. What is the MOST appropriate action for the IS auditor to take?

options.A: Develop an alternate testing procedure.
options.B: Report the finding to management.
options.C: perform a walkthrough of the change management process.
options.D: Create additional sample data to test additional changes.

questions.correct_explanation: If a sample-size objective cannot be met with the given data, the information systems (IS) auditor cannot provide assurance regarding the testing objective. In this instance, the IS auditor should develop (with audit management approval) an alternate testing procedure.

wrong_explanations.B: There is not enough evidence to report the finding as a deficiency.
wrong_explanations.C: A walkthrough should not be initiated until an analysis is performed to confirm that this can provide the required assurance.
wrong_explanations.D: It is not appropriate for an IS auditor to create sample data for the purpose of the audit.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: Which of the following situations can impair the independence of an information systems (IS) auditor? The IS auditor:

options.A: implemented specific functionality during the development of an application.
options.B: designed an embedded audit module for auditing an application.
options.C: participated as a member of an application project team and did not have operational responsibilities.
options.D: provided consulting advice concerning application good practices.

questions.correct_explanation: Independence may be impaired if an information systems (IS) auditor is, or was, actively involved in the development, acquisition and implementation of the application system.

wrong_explanations.B: Designing an embedded audit module does not impair an IS auditor's independence.
wrong_explanations.C: IS auditors should not audit work that they have done, but just participating as a member of the application system project team does not impair an IS auditor's independence.
wrong_explanations.D: An IS auditor's independence is not impaired by providing advice on known good practices.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: The PRIMARY advantage of a continuous audit approach is that it:

options.A: does not require an information systems (IS) auditor to collect evidence on system reliability while processing is taking place.
options.B: allows the IS auditor to review and follow up on audit issues in a timely manner.
options.C: places the responsibility for enforcement and monitoring of controls on the security department instead of audit.
options.D: simplifies the extraction and correlation of data from multiple and complex systems.

questions.correct_explanation: Continuous audit allows audit and response to audit issues in a timely manner because audit findings are gathered in near real time.

wrong_explanations.A: The continuous audit approach often requires an information systems (IS) auditor to collect evidence on system reliability while processing is taking place.
wrong_explanations.C: Responsibility for enforcement and monitoring of controls is primarily the responsibility of management.
wrong_explanations.D: The use of continuous audit is not based on the complexity or number of systems being monitored.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: Which of the following impairs the independence of a quality assurance (QA) team?

options.A: Ensuring compliance with development methods
options.B: Checking the test assumptions
options.C: Correcting coding errors during the testing process
options.D: Checking the code to ensure proper documentation

questions.correct_explanation: Correction of code should not be a responsibility of the QA team, because it does not ensure separation of duties and impairs the team's independence.

wrong_explanations.A: Ensuring compliance with development methods is a valid quality assurance (QA) function.
wrong_explanations.B: Checking the test assumptions is a valid QA function.
wrong_explanations.D: Checking the code to ensure proper documentation is a valid QA function.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: In planning an information systems (IS) audit, the MOST critical step is the identification of the:

options.A: areas of significant risk.
options.B: skill sets of the audit staff.
options.C: test steps in the audit.
options.D: time allotted for the audit.

questions.correct_explanation: When designing a risk-based audit plan, it is important to identify the areas of highest risk to determine the areas to be audited.

wrong_explanations.B: The skill sets of the audit staff should have been considered before deciding and selecting the audit. Where the skills are inadequate, the organization should consider using external resources.
wrong_explanations.C: Test steps for the audit are not as critical during the audit planning process as identifying the areas of risk that should be audited.
wrong_explanations.D: The time allotted for an audit is determined during the planning process based on the areas to be audited and is primarily based on the requirement for conducting an appropriate audit.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: The MOST effective audit practice to determine whether controls accurately support the operational effectiveness of transaction processing is:

options.A: control design testing.
options.B: substantive testing.
options.C: inspection of relevant documentation.
options.D: perform tests on risk prevention.

questions.correct_explanation: Among other methods, such as document review or walkthrough, tests of controls are the most effective procedures to assess whether controls accurately support operational effectiveness.

wrong_explanations.A: Testing of control design assesses whether the control is structured to meet a specific control objective. It does not help determine whether the control is operating effectively.
wrong_explanations.C: Control documents may not always describe the actual process in an accurate manner. Therefore, auditors relying on document review have limited assurance that the control is operating as intended.
wrong_explanations.D: Performing tests on risk prevention is considered compliance testing. This type of testing is used to determine whether policies are adhered to.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: The extent to which data will be collected during an information systems (IS) audit should be determined based on the:

options.A: availability of critical and required information.
options.B: auditor's familiarity with the circumstances.
options.C: auditee's ability to find relevant evidence.
options.D: purpose and scope of the audit being done.

questions.correct_explanation: The extent to which data will be collected during an IS audit should be related directly to the scope and purpose of the audit. An IS audit with a narrow purpose and scope, or just a high-level review, will most likely require less data collection than an audit with a wider purpose and scope.

wrong_explanations.A: The extent to which data will be collected during an information systems (IS) audit should be based on the scope, purpose and requirements of the audit and not be constrained by the ease of obtaining the information or by the IS auditor's familiarity with the area being audited.
wrong_explanations.B: An IS auditor must be objective and thorough and not subject to audit risk through preconceived expected results based on familiarity with the area being audited.
wrong_explanations.C: Collecting all the required evidence is a required element of an IS audit, and the scope of the audit should not be limited by the auditee's ability to find relevant evidence. If evidence is not readily available, the auditor must ensure that other forms of audit are considered to ensure compliance in the area that is subject to audit.

tips: Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: While planning an information systems (IS) audit, an assessment of risk should be made to provide:

options.A: reasonable assurance that the audit will cover material items.
options.B: definite assurance that material items will be covered during the audit work.
options.C: reasonable assurance that all items will be covered by the audit.
options.D: sufficient assurance that all items will be covered during the audit work.

questions.correct_explanation: ISACA Information Systems (IS) Audit and Assurance Performance Guideline 2201 (Risk Assessment in Planning) states that the applied risk assessment approach should help with the prioritization and scheduling process of the IS audit and assurance work. The risk assessment should support the selection process of areas and items of audit interest and the decision process to design and conduct particular IS audit engagements.
questions.framework_ref: ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Guideline 2201

wrong_explanations.B: Definite assurance that material items will be covered during the audit work is an impractical proposition.
wrong_explanations.C: Reasonable assurance that all items will be covered during the audit work is not the correct answer, because primarily material items need to be covered, not all items.
wrong_explanations.D: Sufficient assurance that all items will be covered is not as important as ensuring that the audit will cover all material items.

tips: Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: The MOST appropriate action for an information systems (IS) auditor to take when shared user accounts are discovered is to:

options.A: inform the audit committee of the potential issue.
options.B: review audit logs for the IDs in question.
options.C: document the finding and explain the risk of using shared IDs.
options.D: request that the IDs be removed from the system.

questions.correct_explanation: An IS auditor's role is to detect and document findings and control deficiencies. Part of the audit report is to explain the reasoning behind the findings. The use of shared IDs is not recommended because it does not allow for accountability of transactions. An IS auditor defers to management to decide how to respond to the findings presented.

wrong_explanations.A: It is not appropriate for an information systems (IS) auditor to report findings to the audit committee before conducting a more detailed review and presenting them to management for a response.
wrong_explanations.B: Review of audit logs would not be useful because shared IDs do not provide for individual accountability.
wrong_explanations.D: It is not the role of an IS auditor to request the removal of IDs from the system.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is conducting a compliance test to determine whether controls support management policies and procedures. The test will assist the IS auditor to determine:

options.A: that the control is operating efficiently.
options.B: that the control is operating as designed.
options.C: the integrity of data controls.
options.D: the reasonableness of financial reporting controls.

questions.correct_explanation: Compliance tests can be used to test the existence and effectiveness of a defined process. Understanding the objective of a compliance test is important. Information systems (IS) auditors want reasonable assurance that the controls on which they are relying are effective. An effective control is one that meets management expectations and objectives.

wrong_explanations.A: It is important that controls operate efficiently, but, in this case, the intent is to ensure that the controls support management policies and procedures. Therefore, the important issue is whether the controls are operating correctly and thereby meeting the control objective.
wrong_explanations.C: Substantive tests, not compliance tests, are associated with data integrity.
wrong_explanations.D: Determining the reasonableness of financial reporting controls is a very narrow answer because it is limited to financial reporting. It meets the objective of determining whether the controls are reasonable but does not ensure that the control is working correctly and thereby supporting management expectations and objectives.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: The vice president of human resources has requested an information systems (IS) audit to identify payroll overpayments for the previous year. Which is the BEST audit technique to use in this situation?

options.A: Generate sample test data
options.B: Generalized audit software
options.C: Integrated test facility
options.D: Embedded audit module

questions.correct_explanation: Generalized audit software features include mathematical computations, stratification, statistical analysis, sequence checking, duplicate checking and recomputations. An information systems (IS) auditor, using generalized audit software, can design appropriate tests to recompute the payroll, thereby determining whether overpayments were made and to whom.

wrong_explanations.A: Test data tests for the existence of controls that might prevent overpayments, but it does not detect specific, previous miscalculations.
wrong_explanations.C: An integrated test facility helps to identify a problem as it occurs but does not detect errors for a previous period.
wrong_explanations.D: An embedded audit module can enable the IS auditor to evaluate a process and gather audit evidence, but it does not detect errors for a previous period.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: During a security audit of IT processes, an information systems (IS) auditor finds that documented security procedures do not exist. The IS auditor should:

options.A: create the procedures document based on the practices.
options.B: issue an opinion of the current state and end the audit.
options.C: conduct compliance testing on available data.
options.D: identify and evaluate existing practices.

questions.correct_explanation: One of the main objectives of an audit is to identify potential risk; therefore, the most proactive approach is to identify and evaluate the existing security practices being followed by the organization and submit the findings and risk to management, with recommendations to document the current controls or enforce the documented procedures.

wrong_explanations.A: Information systems (IS) auditors should not prepare documentation, because the process may not be compliant with management objectives and doing so can jeopardize their independence.
wrong_explanations.B: Ending the audit and issuing an opinion does not address identification of potential risk. The auditor should evaluate the practices in place. The recommendation may still be for the organization to develop written procedures. Terminating the audit may prevent achieving one of the basic audit objectivesidentification of potential risk.
wrong_explanations.C: Because there are no documented procedures, there is no basis against which to test compliance.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: During a risk analysis, an information systems (IS) auditor identifies threats and potential impacts. Next, the IS auditor should:

options.A: ensure that the risk assessment is aligned to management's risk assessment process.
options.B: identify information assets and the underlying systems.
options.C: disclose the threats and impacts to management.
options.D: identify and evaluate the existing controls.

questions.correct_explanation: It is important for an IS auditor to identify and evaluate the existence and effectiveness of existing and planned controls so that the risk level can be calculated after the potential threats and possible impacts are identified.

wrong_explanations.A: An audit risk assessment is conducted for purposes that are different from management's risk assessment process purposes.
wrong_explanations.B: It is impossible to determine impact without first identifying the assets affected; therefore, this must already have been completed.
wrong_explanations.C: Upon completion of a risk assessment, an information systems (IS) auditor should describe and discuss with management the threats and potential impacts on the assets, and recommendations for addressing the risk. However, this action cannot be done until the controls are identified and the likelihood of the threat is calculated.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following would normally be the MOST reliable evidence for an information systems (IS) auditor?

options.A: A confirmation letter received from a third party verifying an account balance
options.B: Assurance from line management that an application is working as designed
options.C: Trend data obtained from Internet sources
options.D: Ratio analysis developed by the IS auditor from reports supplied by line management

questions.correct_explanation: Evidence obtained from independent third parties is almost always considered to be more reliable than assurance provided by local management.

wrong_explanations.B: Because management is not objective and may not understand the risk and control environment, and it is only providing evidence that the application is working correctly (not the controls), management assurance is not an acceptable level of trust for audit evidence.
wrong_explanations.C: Data collected from the Internet is not always trustworthy or independently validated.
wrong_explanations.D: Ratio analysis can identify trends and deviations from a baseline but is not reliable evidence.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: When evaluating the collective effect of preventive, detective and corrective controls within a process, an information systems (IS) auditor should be aware of which of the following?

options.A: The point at which controls are exercised as data flow through the system.
options.B: Only preventive and detective controls are relevant.
options.C: Corrective controls are regarded as compensating.
options.D: Classification allows an IS auditor to determine the controls that are missing.

questions.correct_explanation: An information systems (IS) auditor should focus on when controls are exercised as data flow through a computer system.

wrong_explanations.B: Corrective controls may also be relevant because they allow an error or problem to be corrected.
wrong_explanations.C: Corrective controls remove or reduce the effects of errors or irregularities and are not exclusively regarded as compensating controls.
wrong_explanations.D: The existence and function of controls are important but not the classification.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which audit technique provides the BEST evidence of the separation of duties in an IT department?

options.A: Discussion with management
options.B: Review of the organization chart
options.C: Observation and interviews
options.D: Testing of user access rights

questions.correct_explanation: Based on the observations and interviews, the information systems (IS) auditor can evaluate the separation of duties. By observing the IT staff performing their tasks, an IS auditor can identify whether they are performing any incompatible operations. By interviewing the IT staff, the auditor can get an overview of the tasks performed.

wrong_explanations.A: Management may not be aware of the detailed functions of each employee in the IT department and whether the controls are being followed. Therefore, discussion with management provides only limited information regarding separation of duties.
wrong_explanations.B: An organization chart does not provide details of the functions of the employees or whether the controls are working correctly.
wrong_explanations.D: Testing of user rights provides information about the rights users have within the information systems but does not provide complete information about the functions they perform. Observation is a better option because user rights can be changed between audits.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: After reviewing the disaster recovery planning process of an organization, an information systems (IS) auditor requests a meeting with organization management to discuss the findings. Which of the following BEST describes the main goal of this meeting?

options.A: Obtain management approval of the corrective action plan.
options.B: Confirm factual accuracy of the findings.
options.C: Assist management in the implementation of corrective actions.
options.D: Prioritize the resolution of the items.

questions.correct_explanation: The goal of the meeting is to confirm the factual accuracy of the audit findings and present an opportunity for management to agree on or respond to recommendations for corrective action.

wrong_explanations.A: Management approval of the corrective action plan is not required. Management can elect to implement another corrective action plan to address the risk.
wrong_explanations.C: Implementation of corrective actions should be done after the factual accuracy of findings is established, but the work of implementing corrective action is not typically assigned to the infol1llation systems (IS) auditor, because this impairs the auditor's independence.
wrong_explanations.D: Rating the audit findings provides guidance to management for allocating resources to the high-risk items first.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor should ensure that review of online electronic funds transfer reconciliation procedures includes:

options.A: vouching.
options.B: authorizations.
options.C: corrections.
options.D: tracing.

questions.correct_explanation: Tracing is a transaction reconciliation effort that involves following the transaction from the original source to its final destination. In electronic funds transfer transactions, the direction on tracing may start from the customer-printed copy of the receipt, proceed to checking the system audit trails and logs, and end with checking the master file records for daily transactions.

wrong_explanations.A: Vouching is usually performed during the funds transfer, not during the reconciliation effort.
wrong_explanations.B: In online processing, authorizations are normally done automatically by the system, not during the reconciliation.
wrong_explanations.C: Correction entries should be reviewed during a reconciliation; however, they are nol1llally done by an individual other than the person entrusted to do reconciliations and are not as important as tracing.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is carrying out a system configuration review. Which of the following is the BEST evidence in support of the current system configuration settings?

options.A: System configuration values that are imported to a spreadsheet by the system administrator
options.B: Standard report with configuration values that are retrieved from the system by the information systems (IS) auditor
options.C: Dated screenshot of the system configuration settings that are made available by the system administrator
options.D: Annual review of approved system configuration values by the business owner

questions.correct_explanation: Evidence that is obtained directly from the source by an IS auditor is more reliable than information that is provided by a system administrator or a business owner because the IS auditor does not have a vested interest in the outcome of the audit.

wrong_explanations.A: Evidence that is not system-generated information can be modified before it is presented to an information systems (IS) auditor. Therefore, it may not be as reliable as evidence that is obtained by the IS auditor. For example, a system administrator can change the settings or modify the graphic image before taking a screenshot.
wrong_explanations.C: The rules may be modified by the administrator prior to taking the screenshot; therefore, this is not the best evidence.
wrong_explanations.D: The annual review provided by a business owner may not reflect current information.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: The purpose of a checksum on an amount field in an electronic data interchange communication of financial transactions is to ensure:

options.A: integrity.
options.B: authenticity.
options.C: authorization.
options.D: nonrepudiation.

questions.correct_explanation: A checksum that is calculated on an amount field and included in the electronic data interchange communication can be used to identify unauthorized modifications.

wrong_explanations.B: Authenticity cannot be established by a checksum alone and needs other controls.
wrong_explanations.C: Authorization cannot be established by a checksum alone and needs other controls.
wrong_explanations.D: Nonrepudiation can be ensured by using digital signatures.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following forms of evidence does an information systems (IS) auditor consider the MOST reliable?

options.A: An oral statement from the auditee
options.B: The results of a test that is performed by an external information systems (IS) auditor
options.C: An internally generated computer accounting report
options.D: A confirmation letter that is received from an outside source

questions.correct_explanation: An independent test that is performed by an IS auditor should always be considered a more reliable source of evidence than a confirmation letter from a third party, because the letter is the result of an analysis of the process and may not be based on authoritative audit techniques. An audit should consist of a combination of inspection, observation and inquiry by an IS auditor as determined by risk. This provides a standard methodology and reasonable assurance that the controls and test results are accurate.

wrong_explanations.A: An oral statement from the auditee is audit evidence but not as reliable as the results of a test that is performed by an external information systems (IS) auditor.
wrong_explanations.C: An internally generated computer accounting report is audit evidence but is not as reliable as the results of a test performed by an external IS auditor.
wrong_explanations.D: An independent test performed by an IS auditor should always be considered a more reliable source of evidence than a confirmation letter from a third party, because a letter is subjective and may not have been generated as a part of an authoritative audit or conform to audit standards.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor who has discovered unauthorized transactions during a review of electronic data interchange (EDI) transactions is likely to recommend improving the:

options.A: EDI trading partner agreements.
options.B: physical controls for terminals.
options.C: authentication techniques for sending and receiving messages.
options.D: program change control procedures.

questions.correct_explanation: Authentication techniques for sending and receiving messages play a key role in minimizing exposure to unauthorized transactions.

wrong_explanations.A: Electronic data interchange trading partner agreements minimize exposure to legal issues but do not resolve the problem of unauthorized transactions.
wrong_explanations.B: Physical control is important and may provide protection from unauthorized people accessing the system but does not provide protection from unauthorized transactions by authorized users.
wrong_explanations.D: Change control procedures do not resolve the issue of unauthorized transactions.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.
When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is validating a control that involves a review of system-generated exception reports. Which of the following is the BEST evidence of the effectiveness of the control?

options.A: Walk-through with the reviewer of the operation of the control
options.B: System-generated exception reports for the review period with the reviewer's sign-off
options.C: A sample system-generated exception report for the review period, with follow-up action items noted by the reviewer
options.D: Management's confirmation of the effectiveness of the control for the review period

questions.correct_explanation: A sample of a system-generated report with evidence that the reviewer followed up on the exceptions represents the best possible evidence of the effective operation of the control, because there is documented evidence that the reviewer reviewed the exception report and took actions based on the exception report.

wrong_explanations.A: walk-through highlights how a control is designed to work, but it seldom highlights the effectiveness of the control, or exceptions or constraints in the process.
wrong_explanations.B: Reviewer sign-off does not demonstrate the effectiveness of the control if the reviewer does not note follow-up actions for the exceptions identified.
wrong_explanations.D: Management's confirmation of effectiveness of the control suffers from lack of independencemanagement might be biased toward the effectiveness of the controls put in place.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An enterprise has recently upgraded its purchase system to incorporate electronic data interchange (EDI) transmissions. Which of the following controls should be implemented in the EDI interface to provide efficient data mapping?

options.A: Key verification
options.B: One-for-one checking
options.C: Manual recalculations
options.D: Functional acknowledgments

questions.correct_explanation: Acting as an audit trail for electronic data interchange transactions, functional acknowledgments are one of the main controls used in data mapping.

wrong_explanations.A: Key verification is used for encryption and protection of data but not for data mapping.
wrong_explanations.B: One-for-one checking validates that transactions are accurate and complete but does not map data.
wrong_explanations.C: Manual recalculations are used to verify that the processing is correct but do not map data.

tips: Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: Which of the following sampling methods is the MOST effective to determine whether purchase orders issued to vendors have been authorized as per the authorization matrix?

options.A: Variable sampling
options.B: Stratified mean per unit
options.C: Attribute sampling
options.D: Unstratified mean per unit

questions.correct_explanation: Attribute sampling is the method used for compliance testing. In this scenario, the operation of a control is being evaluated, and therefore, the attribute of whether each purchase order was correctly authorized would be used to determine compliance with the control.

wrong_explanations.A: Variable sampling is the method used for substantive testing, which involves testing transactions for quantitative aspects such as monetary values.
wrong_explanations.B: Stratified mean per unit is used in variable sampling.
wrong_explanations.D: Unstratified mean per unit is used in variable sampling.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: The BEST method of confirming the accuracy of a system tax calculation is by:

options.A: review and analysis of the source code of the calculation programs.
options.B: recreating program logic using generalized audit software to calculate monthly totals.
options.C: preparing simulated transactions for processing and comparing the results to predetermined results.
options.D: automatic flowcharting and analysis of the source code of the calculation programs.

questions.correct_explanation: Preparing simulated transactions for processing and comparing the results to predetermined results is the best method for confirming the accuracy of a tax calculation.

wrong_explanations.A: A review of source code is not an effective method of ensuring that the calculation is being computed correctly.
wrong_explanations.B: Recreating program logic may lead to errors, and monthly totals are not accurate enough to ensure correct computations.
wrong_explanations.D: Flowcharting and analysis of source code are not effective methods to address the accuracy of individual tax calculations.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Watch for separation-of-duties violations: the same actor authorizing AND executing, designing AND testing, or developing AND deploying.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor performing a review of application controls evaluates the:

options.A: efficiency of the application in meeting the business processes.
options.B: impact of any exposures discovered.
options.C: business processes served by the application.
options.D: application optimization.

questions.correct_explanation: An application control review involves the evaluation of the application automated controls and an assessment of any exposures resulting from the control weaknesses.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing the effectiveness of the controls, not the suitability of the application to meet business needs.
wrong_explanations.C: The other choices may be objectives of an application audit but are not part of an audit restricted to a review of the application controls.
wrong_explanations.D: One area to be reviewed may be the efficiency and optimization of the application, but this is not the area being reviewed in this audit.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Corrective action has been taken by an auditee immediately after the identification of a reportable finding. The information systems (IS) auditor should:

options.A: include the finding in the final report because the IS auditor is responsible for an accurate report of all findings.
options.B: not include the finding in the final report because management resolved the item.
options.C: not include the finding in the final report because corrective action can be verified by the IS auditor during the audit.
options.D: include the finding in the closing meeting for discussion purposes only.

questions.correct_explanation: Including the finding in the final report is a generally accepted audit practice. If an action is taken after the audit started and before it ended, the audit report should identify the finding and describe the corrective action taken. An audit report should reflect the situation, as it existed at the start of the audit. All corrective actions taken by the auditee should be reported in writing.

wrong_explanations.B: The audit report should contain all relevant findings and the response from management even if the finding has been resolved. This means that subsequent audits may test for the continued resolution of the control.
wrong_explanations.C: The audit report should contain the finding so that it is documented and the removal of the control subsequent to the audit is noticed.
wrong_explanations.D: The audit report should contain the finding and resolution, and this can be mentioned in the final meeting. The audit report should list all relevant findings and the response from management.

tips: When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: The internal information systems (IS) audit team is auditing controls over sales returns and is concerned about fraud. Which of the following sampling methods will BEST assist the IS auditors?

options.A: Stop-or-go
options.B: Classical variable
options.C: Discovery
options.D: Probability-proportional-to-size

questions.correct_explanation: Discovery sampling is used when an information systems (IS) auditor is trying to determine whether a type of event has occurred. Therefore, it is suited to assess the risk of fraud and to identify whether a single occurrence has taken place.

wrong_explanations.A: Stop-or-go is a sampling method that helps limit the size of a sample and allows the test to be stopped at the earliest possible moment.
wrong_explanations.B: Classical variable sampling is associated with dollar amounts and has a sample based on a representative sample of the population but is not focused on fraud.
wrong_explanations.D: Probability-proportional-to-size sampling is typically associated with cluster sampling when there are groups within a sample. The question does not indicate that an IS auditor is searching for a threshold of fraud.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: When developing a risk-based audit strategy, an information systems (IS) auditor should conduct a risk assessment to ensure that:

options.A: controls needed to mitigate risk are in place.
options.B: vulnerabilities and threats are identified.
options.C: audit risk is considered.
options.D: a gap analysis is appropriate.

questions.correct_explanation: While developing a risk-based audit strategy, it is critical that the risk and vulnerabilities are understood. They determine the areas to be audited and the extent of coverage.

wrong_explanations.A: Determination of whether appropriate controls that are required to mitigate risk are in place is a result of an audit.
wrong_explanations.C: Audit risk is an inherent aspect of auditing, directly related to the audit process and not relevant to the risk analysis of the environment to be audited.
wrong_explanations.D: A gap analysis is normally done to compare the actual state to an expected or desirable state.

tips: Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: During an exit interview, in cases where there is disagreement regarding the impact of a finding, an information systems (IS) auditor should:

options.A: ask the auditee to sign a release form accepting full legal responsibility.
options.B: elaborate on the significance of the finding and the risk of not correcting it.
options.C: report the disagreement to the audit committee for resolution.
options.D: accept the auditee position because they are the process owners.

questions.correct_explanation: if the auditee disagrees with the impact of a finding, it is important for an IS auditor to elaborate and clarify the risk and exposures because the auditee may not fully appreciate the magnitude of the exposure. The goal should be to enlighten the auditee or uncover new information of which an IS auditor may not have been aware. Anything that appears to threaten the auditee lessens effective communications and sets up an adversarial relationship, but an IS auditor should not automatically agree just because the auditee expresses an alternate point of view.

wrong_explanations.A: Management is always responsible and liable for risk. The role of the information systems (IS) auditor is to inform management of the findings and associated risk discovered in an audit.
wrong_explanations.C: The audit report contains the finding from the IS auditor and the response from management. It is the responsibility of management to accept risk or mitigate it appropriately. The role of the auditor is to inform management clearly and thoroughly so that the best decision can be made.
wrong_explanations.D: The IS auditor must be professional, competent and independent. They must not just accept an explanation or argument from management, unless the process used to generate the finding was flawed.

tips: When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: To ensure that audit resources deliver the best value to the organization, the FIRST step in an audit project is to:

options.A: schedule the audits and monitor the time spent on each audit.
options.B: train the information systems (IS) audit staff on current technology used in the organization.
options.C: develop the audit plan based on a detailed risk assessment.
options.D: monitor progress of audits and initiate cost control measures.

questions.correct_explanation: Although monitoring the time and audit programs, and adequate training improve the IS audit staff's productivity (efficiency and performance), ensuring that the resources and efforts being dedicated to audit are focused on higher-risk areas delivers value to the organization.

wrong_explanations.A: Monitoring the audits and the time spent on audits is not effective if the wrong areas are being audited. It is most important to develop a risk-based audit plan to ensure effective use of audit resources.
wrong_explanations.B: The information systems (IS) auditor may have specialties, or the audit team may rely on outside experts to conduct very specialized audits. It is not necessary for each IS auditor to be trained on all new technology.
wrong_explanations.D: Monitoring audits and initiating cost controls does not ensure the effective use of audit resources.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).
Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: Which of the following should be the FIRST action of an information systems (IS) auditor during a dispute with a department manager over audit findings?

options.A: Retest the control to validate the finding.
options.B: Engage a third party to validate the finding.
options.C: Include the finding in the report with the department manager's comments.
options.D: Revalidate the supporting evidence for the finding.

questions.correct_explanation: Conclusions drawn by an IS auditor should be adequately supported by evidence, and any compensating controls or corrections that are pointed out by a department manager should be taken into consideration. Therefore, the first step is to revalidate the evidence for the finding. If, after revalidating and retesting, there are unsettled disagreements, those issues should be included in the report.

wrong_explanations.A: Retesting the control normally occurs after the evidence has been revalidated.
wrong_explanations.B: Although there are cases where a third party may be needed to perform specialized audit procedures, an information systems (IS) auditor should first revalidate the supporting evidence to determine whether there is a need to engage a third party.
wrong_explanations.C: Before putting a disputed finding or management response in the audit report, the IS auditor should take care to review the evidence that is used in the finding to ensure audit accuracy.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor should use statistical sampling when:

options.A: the probability of error must be objectively quantified.
options.B: the auditor wants to avoid sampling risk.
options.C: generalized audit software is unavailable.
options.D: the tolerable error rate cannot be determined.

questions.correct_explanation: Given an expected error rate and confidence level, statistical sampling is an objective method of sampling that helps an information systems (IS) auditor determine the sample size and quantify the probability of error (confidence coefficient).

wrong_explanations.B: Sampling risk is the risk of a sample not being representative of the population. This risk exists for judgment and statistical samples.
wrong_explanations.C: Statistical sampling can use generalized audit software, but it is not required.
wrong_explanations.D: The tolerable error rate must be predetermined for both judgment and statistical sampling.

tips: Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: What is the BEST action for an information systems (IS) auditor to take when an outsourced monitoring process for remote access is inadequate and management disagrees because intrusion detection system (IDS) and firewall controls are in place?

options.A: Revise the finding in the audit report per management's feedback.
options.B: Retract the finding because the IDS controls are in place.
options.C: Retract the finding because the firewall rules are monitored.
options.D: Document the identified finding in the audit report.

questions.correct_explanation: IS auditor independence dictates that the additional information provided by the auditee is taken into consideration. Normally, an IS auditor does not automatically retract or revise the finding.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor may include the management response in the report, but that will not affect the requirement to report the finding.
wrong_explanations.B: The finding remains valid and the management response is documented; however, the audit may indicate a need to review the validity of the management response.
wrong_explanations.C: The finding remains valid and the management response is documented; however, the audit may indicate a need to review the validity of the management response.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: An organization uses a bank to process its weekly payroll. Time sheets and payroll adjustment forms (e.g., hourly rate changes and terminations) are completed and delivered to the bank, which prepares the checks and reports for distribution. To BEST ensure payroll data accuracy:

options.A: payroll reports should be compared to input forms.
options.B: gross payroll should be recalculated manually.
options.C: checks should be compared to input forms.
options.D: checks should be reconciled with output reports.

questions.correct_explanation: The best way to confirm data accuracy, when input is provided by the organization and output is generated by the bank, is to verify the data input (input forms) with the results of the payroll reports.

wrong_explanations.B: Recalculating gross payroll manually only verifies whether the processing is correct and not the data accuracy of inputs.
wrong_explanations.C: Comparing checks to input forms is not feasible because checks contain the processed information and input forms contain the input data.
wrong_explanations.D: Reconciling checks with output reports only confirms that checks were issued as stated on output reports.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Watch for separation-of-duties violations: the same actor authorizing AND executing, designing AND testing, or developing AND deploying.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the GREATEST potential risk in an electronic data interchange (EDI) environment?

options.A: Lack of transaction authorizations
options.B: Loss or duplication of EDI transmissions
options.C: Transmission delay
