options.D: Deletion or manipulation of transactions prior to, or after, establishment of application controls

questions.correct_explanation: Because the interaction between parties is electronic, there is no inherent authentication occurring; therefore, lack of transaction authorization is the greatest risk.

wrong_explanations.B: Loss or duplication of electronic data interchange transmissions is an example of risk, but because all transactions should be logged, the impact is not as great as that of unauthorized transactions.
wrong_explanations.C: Transmission delays may terminate the process or hold the line until the normal time for processing has elapsed; however, there will be no loss of data.
wrong_explanations.D: Deletion or manipulation of transactions prior to, or after, establishment of application controls is an example of risk. Logging detects any alteration to the data, and the impact is not as great as that of unauthorized transactions.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: During the planning stage of an information systems (IS) audit, the PRIMARY goal of an IS auditor is to:

options.A: address audit objectives.
options.B: collect sufficient evidence.
options.C: specify appropriate tests.
options.D: minimize audit resources.

questions.correct_explanation: ISACA Information Systems (IS) Audit and Assurance Standards require that an IS auditor plan the audit work to address the audit objectives. The activities described in the other options are all undertaken to address audit objectives and, thus, are secondary.
questions.framework_ref: ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Standards

wrong_explanations.B: The IS auditor does not collect evidence in the planning stage of an audit.
wrong_explanations.C: Specifying appropriate tests is not the primary goal of audit planning.
wrong_explanations.D: Effective use of audit resources is a goal of audit planning, not minimizing audit resources.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: When selecting audit procedures, an information systems (IS) auditor should use professional judgment to ensure that:

options.A: sufficient evidence will be collected.
options.B: significant deficiencies will be corrected within a reasonable period.
options.C: all material weaknesses will be identified.
options.D: audit costs will be kept at a minimum level.

questions.correct_explanation: Procedures are processes that an information systems (IS) auditor may follow in an audit engagement. In determining the appropriateness of any specific procedure, an IS auditor should use professional judgment that is appropriate to the specific circumstances. Professional judgment involves a subjective and often qualitative evaluation of conditions arising during an audit. Judgment addresses a grey area where binary (yes/no) decisions are not appropriate, and the IS auditor's past experience plays a key role in making a judgment. The IS auditor should use judgment in assessing the sufficiency of evidence to be collected. ISACA guidelines provide information on how to meet the standards when performing IS audit work.

wrong_explanations.B: The correction of deficiencies is the responsibility of management and is not a part of the audit procedure selection process.
wrong_explanations.C: Identifying material weaknesses is the result of appropriate competence, experience and thoroughness in planning and executing the audit, and not of professional judgment. Professional judgment is not a primary input to the financial aspects of the audit. Audit procedures and use of professional judgment cannot ensure that all deficiencies/weaknesses will be identified and corrected.
wrong_explanations.D: Professional judgment ensures that audit resources and costs are used wisely, but this is not the primary objective of the auditor when selecting audit procedures.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: A substantive test to verify that tape library inventory records are accurate is:

options.A: determining whether bar code readers are installed.
options.B: determining whether the movement of tapes is authorized.
options.C: conducting a physical count of the tape inventory.
options.D: checking whether receipts and issues of tapes are accurately recorded.

questions.correct_explanation: A substantive test includes gathering evidence to evaluate the integrity (i.e., the completeness, accuracy and validity) of individual transactions, data or other information. Conducting a physical count of the tape inventory is a substantive test.

wrong_explanations.A: Determining whether bar code readers are installed is a compliance test.
wrong_explanations.B: Determining whether the movement of tapes is authorized is a compliance test.
wrong_explanations.D: Checking whether receipts and issues of tapes are accurately recorded is a compliance test.

tips: Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An appropriate control for ensuring the authenticity of orders received in an electronic data interchange system application is to:

options.A: acknowledge receipt of electronic orders with a confirmation message.
options.B: perform reasonableness checks on quantities ordered before filling orders.
options.C: verify the identity of senders and determine if orders correspond to contract terms.
options.D: encrypt electronic orders.

questions.correct_explanation: An electronic data interchange system is subject not only to the usual risk exposures of computer systems but also to those arising from the potential ineffectiveness of controls on the part of the trading partner and the third-party service provider, making authentication of users and messages a major security concern.

wrong_explanations.A: Acknowledging the receipt of electronic orders with a confirming message is good practice but will not authenticate orders from customers.
wrong_explanations.B: Performing reasonableness checks on quantities ordered before placing orders is a control for ensuring the correctness of the orders, not the authenticity of its customer orders.
wrong_explanations.D: Encrypting sensitive messages is an appropriate step but does not prove authenticity of messages received.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor finds that the answers received during an interview with a payroll clerk do not support job descriptions and documented procedures. Under these circumstances, the IS auditor should:

options.A: conclude that the controls are inadequate.
options.B: expand the scope to include substantive testing.
options.C: place greater reliance on previous audits.
options.D: suspend the audit.

questions.correct_explanation: if the answers provided to an IS auditor's questions are not confirmed by documented procedures or job descriptions, the IS auditor should expand the scope of testing the controls and include additional substantive tests.

wrong_explanations.A: Based solely on the interview with the payroll clerk, the information systems (IS) auditor will not be able to collect evidence to determine the adequacy of existing controls.
wrong_explanations.C: Placing greater reliance on previous audits is an inappropriate action because it provides no current knowledge of the adequacy of the existing controls.
wrong_explanations.D: Suspending the audit is an inappropriate action because it provides no current knowledge of the adequacy of the existing controls.

tips: Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An external information systems (IS) auditor issues an audit report pointing out the lack of firewall protection features at the perimeter network gateway and recommending a specific vendor product to address this vulnerability. The IS auditor has failed to exercise:

options.A: professional independence.
options.B: organizational independence.
options.C: technical competence.
options.D: professional competence.

questions.correct_explanation: When an information systems (IS) auditor recommends a specific vendor, the auditor's professional independence is compromised.

wrong_explanations.B: Organizational independence has no relevance to the content of an audit report and should be considered at the time of accepting the engagement.
wrong_explanations.C: Technical competence is not relevant to the requirement of independence.
wrong_explanations.D: Professional competence is not relevant to the requirement of independence.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: The PRIMARY reason an information systems (IS) auditor performs a functional walk-through during the preliminary phase of an audit assignment is to:

options.A: understand the business process.
options.B: comply with auditing standards.
options.C: identify control weakness.
options.D: develop the risk assessment.

questions.correct_explanation: Understanding the business process is the first step that an information systems (IS) auditor needs to perform.
questions.framework_ref: ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Standards

wrong_explanations.B: ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Standards encourage adoption of the audit procedures/processes required to assist the IS auditor in performing IS audits more effectively. However, standards do not require an IS auditor to perform a process walk-through at the commencement of an audit engagement.
wrong_explanations.C: Identifying control weaknesses is not the primary reason for the walk-through and typically occurs at a later stage in the audit.
wrong_explanations.D: The main reason is to understand the business process. The risk assessment is developed after the business process is understood.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: In the process of evaluating program change controls, an information systems (IS) auditor uses source code comparison software to:

options.A: examine source program changes without information from IS personnel.
options.B: detect a source program change made between acquiring a copy of the source and the comparison run.
options.C: confirm that the control copy is the current version of the production program.
options.D: ensure that all changes made in the current source copy are tested.

questions.correct_explanation: When an information systems (IS) auditor uses a source code comparison to examine source program changes without information from IS personnel, the IS auditor has an objective, independent and relatively complete assurance of program changes because the source code comparison identifies the changes.

wrong_explanations.B: The changes detected by the source code comparison are between two versions of the software. This does not detect changes made since the acquisition of the copy of the software.
wrong_explanations.C: This is a function of library management, not source code comparison. An IS auditor gains this assurance separately.
wrong_explanations.D: Source code comparison detects all changes between an original and a changed program; however, the comparison will not ensure that the changes have been adequately tested.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: The PRIMARY purpose for meeting with auditees prior to formally closing a review is to:

options.A: confirm that the auditors did not overlook any important issues.
options.B: gain agreement on the findings.
options.C: receive feedback on the adequacy of the audit procedures.
options.D: test the structure of the final presentation.

questions.correct_explanation: The primary purpose for meeting with auditees prior to formally closing a review is to gain agreement on the findings and responses from management.

wrong_explanations.A: The closing meeting identifies any misunderstandings or errors in the audit but does not identify any important issues overlooked in the audit.
wrong_explanations.C: The closing meeting may obtain comments from management on the conduct of the audit but is not intended to be a formal review of the adequacy of the audit procedures.
wrong_explanations.D: The structure of an audit report and the presentation follows accepted standards and practices. The closing meeting may indicate errors in the audit or presentation but is not intended to test the structure of the presentation.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: Which of the following audit techniques BEST helps an information systems (IS) auditor to determine whether unauthorized program changes have been made since the last authorized program update?

options.A: Test data run
options.B: Code review
options.C: Automated code comparison
options.D: Review of code migration procedures

questions.correct_explanation: An automated code comparison is the process of comparing two versions of the same program to determine whether the two correspond. It is an efficient technique because it is an automated procedure.

wrong_explanations.A: Test data runs permit the auditor to verify the processing of preselected trans.actions but provide no evidence about unauthorized changes or unexercised portions of a program.
wrong_explanations.B: Code review is the process of reading program source code listings to determine whether the code follows coding standards or contains potential errors or inefficient statements. A code review can be used as a means of code comparison, but it is inefficient and unlikely to detect any changes in the code, especially in a large program.
wrong_explanations.D: The review of code migration procedures does not detect unauthorized program changes.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: When preparing an audit report, the information systems (IS) auditor should ensure that the results are supported by:

options.A: statements from IS management.
options.B: work papers of other auditors.
options.C: an organizational control self-assessment.
options.D: sufficient and appropriate audit evidence.

questions.correct_explanation: ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Reporting Standards require that the IS auditor has sufficient and appropriate audit evidence to support the reported results. Statements from IS management provide a basis for obtaining concurrence on matters that cannot be verified with empirical evidence. The report should be based on evidence that is collected during the review even though the IS auditor may have access to the work papers of other auditors. The results of an organizational control self-assessment can supplement the audit findings.
questions.framework_ref: ISACA IS Audit and Assurance Reporting Standards

wrong_explanations.A: Statements from information systems (IS) management may be included in the audit analysis but these statements alone are not considered a sufficient basis for issuing a report.
wrong_explanations.B: Work papers from other auditors may be used to substantiate and validate a finding but should not be used without the additional evidence of the work papers from the IS auditor who is preparing the report.
wrong_explanations.C: The results of a control self-assessment may assist the IS auditor in determining risk and compliance but on its own is not enough to support the audit report.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: While evaluating software development practices in an organization, an information systems (IS) auditor notes that the quality assurance (QA) function reports to project management. The MOST important concern for an IS auditor is the:

options.A: effectiveness of the QA function because it should interact between project management and user management.
options.B: efficiency of the QA function because it should interact with the project implementation team.
options.C: effectiveness of the project manager because the project manager should interact with the QA function.
options.D: efficiency of the project manager because the QA function needs to communicate with the project implementation team.

questions.correct_explanation: To be effective, the quality assurance (QA) function should be independent of project management. Ifit is not, project management may put pressure on the QA function to approve an inadequate product.

wrong_explanations.B: The efficiency of the QA function is not impacted by interacting with the project implementation team. The QA team does not release a product for implementation until it meets QA requirements.
wrong_explanations.C: The project manager responds to the issues raised by the QA team. This does not impact the effectiveness of the project manager.
wrong_explanations.D: The QA function interaction with the project implementation team should not impact the efficiency of the project manager.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: The final decision to include a material finding in an audit report should be made by the:

options.A: audit committee.
options.B: auditee's manager.
options.C: information systems (IS) auditor.
options.D: chief executive officer.

questions.correct_explanation: The IS auditor should make the final decision about what to include or exclude from the audit report.

wrong_explanations.A: The audit committee should not impair the independence, professionalism and objectivity of the information systems (IS) auditor by influencing what is included in the audit report.
wrong_explanations.B: The IS auditor's manager may recommend what should or should not be included in an audit report, but the auditee's manager should not influence the content of the report.
wrong_explanations.D: The chief executive officer must not provide influence over the content of an audit report because that would be a breach of the independence of the audit function.

tips: When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: While reviewing sensitive electronic work papers, the information systems (IS) auditor notices that they were not encrypted. This could compromise the:

options.A: audit trail of the versioning of the work papers.
options.B: approval of the audit phases.
options.C: access rights to the work papers.
options.D: confidentiality of the work papers.

questions.correct_explanation: Encryption provides confidentiality for electronic work papers.

wrong_explanations.A: Audit trails do not, by themselves, affect confidentiality, but are part of the reason for requiring encryption.
wrong_explanations.B: Audit phase approvals do not, by themselves, affect the confidentiality of the work papers, but are part of the reason for requiring encryption.
wrong_explanations.C: Access to the work papers should be limited by need to know; however, a lack of encryption breaches the confidentiality of the work papers, not the access rights to the papers.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: The MOST important reason for an information systems (IS) auditor to obtain sufficient and appropriate audit evidence is to:

options.A: comply with regulatory requirements.
options.B: provide a basis for drawing reasonable conclusions.
options.C: ensure complete audit coverage.
options.D: perform the audit according to the defined scope.

questions.correct_explanation: The scope of an information systems (IS) audit is defined by its objectives. This involves identifying control weaknesses relevant to the scope of the audit. Obtaining sufficient and appropriate evidence assists the auditor in not only identifying control weaknesses but also documenting and validating them.

wrong_explanations.A: Complying with regulatory requirements is relevant to an audit but is not the most important reason why sufficient and relevant evidence is required.
wrong_explanations.C: Ensuring coverage is relevant to conducting an IS audit but is not the most important reason why sufficient and relevant evidence is required. The reason for obtaining evidence is to ensure that the audit conclusions are factual and accurate.
wrong_explanations.D: The execution of an audit to meet its defined scope is relevant to an audit but is not the reason why sufficient and relevant evidence is required.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: After initial investigation, an information systems (IS) auditor has reasons to believe that fraud may be present. The IS auditor should:

options.A: expand activities to determine whether an investigation is warranted.
options.B: report the matter to the audit committee.
options.C: report the possibility of fraud to management.
options.D: consult with external legal counsel to determine the course of action to be taken.

questions.correct_explanation: An information systems (IS) auditor's responsibilities for detecting fraud include evaluating fraud indicators, and deciding whether any additional action is necessary or whether an investigation should be recommended.

wrong_explanations.B: The IS auditor should notify the appropriate authorities within the organization only if it has determined that the indicators of fraud are sufficient to recommend an investigation.
wrong_explanations.C: The IS auditor should report the possibility of fraud to top management only after there is sufficient evidence to launch an investigation. This may be affected by whether management may be involved in the fraud.
wrong_explanations.D: Normally, the IS auditor does not have authority to consult with external legal counsel.

tips: Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor notes that failed login attempts to a core financial system are automatically logged and the logs are retained for a year by the organization. This logging is:

options.A: an effective preventive control.
options.B: a valid detective control.
options.C: not an adequate control.
options.D: a corrective control.

questions.correct_explanation: Generation of an activity log is not a control by itself. It is the review of such a log that makes the activity a control (i.e., generation plus review equals control).

wrong_explanations.A: Generation of an activity log is not a preventive control because it cannot prevent inappropriate access.
wrong_explanations.B: Generation of an activity log is not a detective control because it does not help in detecting inappropriate access unless it is reviewed by appropriate personnel.
wrong_explanations.D: Generation of an activity log is not a corrective control because it does not correct the effect of inappropriate access.

tips: Watch for separation-of-duties violations: the same actor authorizing AND executing, designing AND testing, or developing AND deploying.

questions.question: An organization's information systems (IS) audit charter should specify the:

options.A: plans for IS audit engagements.
options.B: objectives and scope of IS audit engagements.
options.C: detailed training plan for the IS audit staff.
options.D: role of the IS audit function.

questions.correct_explanation: An IS audit charter establishes the role of the information systems audit function. The charter should describe the overall authority, scope and responsibilities of the audit function. The charter should be approved by the highest level of management and, if available, by the audit committee.

wrong_explanations.A: Planning is the responsibility of audit management.
wrong_explanations.B: The objectives and scope of each information systems (IS) audit should be agreed on in an engagement letter. The charter specifies the objectives and scope of the audit function but not of individual engagements.
wrong_explanations.C: A training plan that is based on the audit plan should be developed by audit management.

tips: Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: Which of the following should an information systems (IS) auditor use to detect duplicate invoice records within an invoice master file?

options.A: Attribute sampling
options.B: Computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs)
options.C: Compliance testing
options.D: Integrated test facility

questions.correct_explanation: Computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs) enable the IS auditor to review the entire invoice file to look for those items that meet the selection criteria.

wrong_explanations.A: Attribute sampling aids in identifying records meeting specific conditions but does not compare one record to another to identify duplicates. To detect duplicate invoice records, the information systems (IS) auditor should check all items that meet the criteria and not just a sample of the items.
wrong_explanations.C: Compliance testing determines whether control procedures are adhered to. Using CAATs is the better option because it is most likely more efficient to search for duplicates.
wrong_explanations.D: An integrated test facility allows the IS auditor to test transactions through the production system but does not compare records to identify duplicates.

tips: Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: When developing a risk management program, what is the FIRST activity to be performed?

options.A: Threat assessment
options.B: Classification of data
options.C: Inventory of assets
options.D: Criticality analysis

questions.correct_explanation: Identification of the assets to be protected is the first step in the development of a risk management program.

wrong_explanations.A: The assets need to be identified first. A listing of the threats that can affect the assets is a later step in the process.
wrong_explanations.B: Data classification is required for defining access controls and in criticality analysis, but the assets (including data) need be identified before doing classification.
wrong_explanations.D: Criticality analysis is a later step in the process after the assets have been identified.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).

questions.question: When evaluating the controls of an electronic data interchange (EDI) application, an information systems (IS) auditor should PRIMARILY be concerned with the risk of:

options.A: excessive transaction turnaround time.
options.B: application interface failure.
options.C: improper transaction authorization.
options.D: nonvalidated batch totals.

questions.correct_explanation: Foremost among the risk associated with electronic data interchange (EDI) is improper transaction authorization. Because the interaction with the parties is electronic, there is no inherent authentication. Improper authentication poses a serious risk of financial loss.

wrong_explanations.A: An excessive turnaround time is an inconvenience, but not a serious risk.
wrong_explanations.B: The failure of the application interface is a risk, but not the most serious issue. Usually such a problem is temporary and easily fixed.
wrong_explanations.D: The integrity of EDI transactions is important, but not as significant as the risk of unauthorized transactions.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following would be MOST useful for an information systems (IS) auditor for accessing and analyzing digital data to collect relevant audit evidence from diverse software environments?

options.A: Structured Query Language (SQL)
options.B: Application software reports
options.C: Data analytics controls
options.D: Computer-assisted auditing techniques (CAATs)

questions.correct_explanation: CAATs are tools used for accessing data in an electronic form from diverse software environments, record formats, etc. CAATs serve as useful tools for collecting and evaluating audit evidence according to audit objectives and can create efficiencies for collecting this evidence.

wrong_explanations.A: Structured Query Language (SQL) provides options for auditors to query specific tables of a database according to audit objectives. However, skills are required to query specific databases, and a user must be able to understand the record structure to access the data.
wrong_explanations.B: Reports from application software may be useful, but they are not as beneficial as computer-assisted auditing techniques (CAATs).
wrong_explanations.C: Data analytics controls might be a good technique to use for control testing, but they are not as comprehensive as CAATs.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: Which of the following sampling methods is the MOST appropriate for testing automated invoice authorization controls to ensure that exceptions are not made for specific users?

options.A: Variable sampling
options.B: Judgmental sampling
options.C: Stratified random sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

questions.correct_explanation: Stratification is the process of dividing a population into subpopulations with similar characteristics explicitly defined, so that each sampling unit can belong to only one stratum. This method of sampling ensures that all sampling units in each subgroup have a known, nonzero chance of selection. It is the most appropriate method in this case.

wrong_explanations.A: Variable sampling is used for substantive testing to determine the monetary or volumetric impact of characteristics of a population. This is not the most appropriate method in this case.
wrong_explanations.B: In judgmental sampling, professionals place a bias on the sample (e.g., all sampling units over a certain value, all for a specific type of exception or all negatives). A judgmental sample is not statistically based, and results should not be extrapolated over the population because the sample is unlikely to be representative of the population.
wrong_explanations.D: Systematic sampling involves selecting sampling units using a fixed interval between selections with the first interval having a random start. This is not the most appropriate method in this case.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor who was involved in designing an organization's business continuity plan (BCP) has been assigned to audit the plan. The IS auditor should:

options.A: decline the assignment.
options.B: inform management of the possible conflict of interest after completing the audit assignment.
options.C: inform the BCP team of the possible conflict of interest prior to beginning the assignment.
options.D: confirm the possibility of conflict of interest to audit management prior to starting the assignment.

questions.correct_explanation: A possible conflict of interest, likely to affect the information systems (IS) auditor's independence, should be brought to the attention of management prior to starting the assignment.

wrong_explanations.A: Declining the assignment can be acceptable only after obtaining management approval or it is appropriately disclosed to management, audit management and other stakeholders.
wrong_explanations.B: Approval should be obtained prior to commencement and not after the completion of the assignment.
wrong_explanations.C: Informing the business continuity plan (BCP) team of the possible conflict of interest prior to starting the assignment is not the correct answer because the BCP team does not have the authority to decide on this issue.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: The PRIMARY purpose of an IT forensic audit is:

options.A: to participate in investigations related to corporate fraud.
options.B: to enable the systematic collection and analysis of evidence after a system irregularity.
options.C: To assess the correctness of an organization's financial statements.
options.D: to preserve evidence of criminal activity.

questions.correct_explanation: The systematic collection and analysis of evidence after a system irregularity best describes a forensic audit. The evidence collected can then be analyzed and used in judicial proceedings.

wrong_explanations.A: Forensic audits are not limited to corporate fraud.
wrong_explanations.C: Assessing the correctness of an organization's financial statements is not the primary purpose of most forensic audits.
wrong_explanations.D: Forensics is the investigation of evidence related to a crime or misbehavior. Preserving evidence is the forensic process, but not the primary purpose.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviews one day of logs for a remotely managed server and finds one case where logging failed, and the backup restarts cannot be confirmed. What should the IS auditor do?

options.A: Issue an audit finding.
options.B: Seek an explanation from IS management.
options.C: Review the classifications of data held on the server.
options.D: Expand the sample of logs reviewed.

questions.correct_explanation: IS Audit and Assurance Standards require that an IS auditor gather sufficient and appropriate audit evidence. The IS auditor found a potential problem and now needs to determine whether this is an isolated incident or a systematic control failure.

wrong_explanations.A: At this stage, it is too preliminary to issue an audit finding. Seeking an explanation from management is advisable, but it is better to gather additional evidence to properly evaluate the seriousness of the situation.
wrong_explanations.B: Without gathering more information on the incident and the frequency of the incident, it is difficult to obtain a meaningful explanation from management.
wrong_explanations.C: A backup failure, which has not been established at this point, is serious if it involves critical data. However, the issue is not the importance of the data on the server, where a problem has been detected, but whether a systematic control failure that impacts other servers exists.

tips: Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: In a small organization, the function of release manager and application programmer are performed by the same employee. What is the BEST compensating control in this scenario?

options.A: Hiring additional staff to provide separation of duties
options.B: Preventing the release manager from making program modifications
options.C: Logging of changes to development libraries
options.D: Verifying that only approved program changes are implemented

questions.correct_explanation: Compensating controls are used to mitigate risk when proper controls are not feasible or practical. In a small organization, it may not be feasible to hire new staff, which is why a compensating control may be necessary. Verifying program changes has roughly the same effect as intended by full separation of duties.

wrong_explanations.A: Establishing separation of duties is not a compensating control; it is a preventive control. In a small organization, it may not be feasible to hire new staff, which is why a compensating control may be necessary.
wrong_explanations.B: Because the release manager is performing dual roles, preventing the release manager from making program modifications is not feasible, and, in a small organization, separation of duties may not be possible.
wrong_explanations.C: Logging changes to development libraries does not detect changes to production libraries.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Watch for separation-of-duties violations: the same actor authorizing AND executing, designing AND testing, or developing AND deploying.

questions.question: Which of the following is the FIRST step in an IT risk assessment for a risk-based audit?

options.A: Identify all IT systems and controls that are relevant to audit objectives.
options.B: List all controls from the audit program to select ones matching with audit objectives.
options.C: Review the results of a risk self-assessment.
options.D: Understand the business, its operating model and key processes.

questions.correct_explanation: Risk-based auditing must be based on an understanding of the business, operating model and environment. This is the first step in an IT risk assessment for a risk-based audit.

wrong_explanations.A: Understanding the business environment comes first; this is followed by understanding the IT environment.
wrong_explanations.B: Listing controls and matching them to audit objectives is not the first step of risk assessment. This step follows understanding the business environment and the IT systems.
wrong_explanations.C: A risk self-assessment is optional and applicable for some types of audit engagements.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).
Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor discovers that devices connected to the network are not included in a network diagram that had been used to develop the scope of the audit. The chief information officer explains that the diagram is being updated and awaiting final approval. The IS auditor should FIRST:

options.A: expand the scope of the IS audit to include the devices that are not on the network diagram.
options.B: evaluate the impact of the undocumented devices on the audit scope.
options.C: note a control deficiency because the network diagram has not been approved.
options.D: plan follow-up audits of the undocumented devices.

questions.correct_explanation: In a risk-based approach to an IS audit, the scope is determined by the impact that the devices will have on the audit. If the undocumented devices do not impact the audit scope, then they may be excluded from the current audit engagement. The information provided on a network diagram can vary depending on what is being illustrated-for example, the network layer and cross connections.

wrong_explanations.A: It is important that the information systems (IS) auditor does not immediately assume that everything on the network diagram provides information about the risk affecting a network/system. There is a process in place for documenting and updating the network diagram.
wrong_explanations.C: In this case, there is simply a mismatch in timing between the completion of the approval process and when the IS audit began. There is no control deficiency to be reported.
wrong_explanations.D: Planning for follow-up audits of the undocumented devices is contingent on the risk that the undocumented devices have on the ability of the entity to meet the audit scope.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).
Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.
Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is testing employee access to a large financial system and selects a sample from the current employee list provided by the auditee. Which of the following evidence is the MOST reliable to support the testing?

options.A: A spreadsheet provided by the system administrator
options.B: Human resources access documents signed by employees' managers
options.C: A list of accounts with access levels generated by the system
options.D: Observations performed onsite in the presence of a system administrator

questions.correct_explanation: The access list generated by the system is the most reliable because it is the most objective evidence to perform a comparison against the samples selected. The evidence is objective because it was generated by the system rather than by an individual.

wrong_explanations.A: A spreadsheet supplied by the system administrator may not be complete or may be inaccurate. Documentary evidence should be collected to support the auditee's spreadsheet.
wrong_explanations.B: The human resources access documents signed by managers are good evidence; however, they are not as objective as the system-generated access list, because access may have changed, or the documents may have been incorrect when they were signed.
wrong_explanations.D: The observations are good evidence to understand the internal control structure; however, observations are not efficient for many users. Observations are not objective enough for substantive tests.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: During a compliance audit of a small bank, the information systems (IS) auditor notes that the IT and accounting functions are being performed by the same user of the financial system. Which of the following reviews that are conducted by the user's supervisor represents the BEST compensating control?

options.A: Audit trails that show the date and time of the transaction
options.B: A daily report with the total numbers and dollar amounts of each transaction
options.C: User account administration
options.D: Computer log files that show individual transactions

questions.correct_explanation: Computer logs record the activities of individuals during their access to a computer system or data file and record any abnormal activities, such as the modification or deletion of financial data.

wrong_explanations.A: An audit trail of only the date and time of the transaction is not sufficient to compensate for the risk of multiple functions being performed by the same individual.
wrong_explanations.B: Review of the summary financial reports does not compensate for the separation of duties issue.
wrong_explanations.C: Supervisor review of user account administration can be a good control; however, it may not detect inappropriate activities where a person fills multiple roles.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: A system developer transfers to the audit department to serve as an IT auditor. When production systems are to be reviewed by this employee, which of the following will become the MOST significant concern?

options.A: The work may be construed as a self-audit.
options.B: Audit points may largely shift to technical aspects.
options.C: The employee may not have sufficient control assessment skills.
options.D: The employee's knowledge of business risk may be limited.

questions.correct_explanation: Because the employee had been a developer, it is recommended that the audit coverage should exclude the systems developed by this employee to avoid any conflicts of interests.

wrong_explanations.B: Because the employee has a technical background, it is possible that the audit findings tend to focus on technical matters. However, this is normally corrected in the review process before it is carried out in production.
wrong_explanations.C: Because auditing is a new role for this employee, they may not have adequate control assessment skills. However, this can be addressed by on-the-job training and is not as big of a concern as a potential conflict of interest.
wrong_explanations.D: Because this employee was previously employed in the organization's IT department, it is possible to build upon the employee's current understanding of the business to address any gaps in knowledge.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the objective of an information systems (IS) auditor discussing the audit findings with the auditee?

options.A: Communicate results to the auditee.
options.B: Develop timelines for the implementation of suggested recommendations.
options.C: Confirm the findings and propose a course of corrective action.
options.D: Identify compensating controls to the identified risk.

questions.correct_explanation: Before communicating the results of an audit to senior management, the IS auditor should discuss the findings with the auditee. The goal of this discussion is to confirm the accuracy of the findings and to propose a course of corrective action.

wrong_explanations.A: Based on this discussion, the information systems (IS) auditor will finalize the report and present the report to relevant levels of senior management after the findings are confirmed. This discussion should, however, also address a timetable for remediation of the audit findings.
wrong_explanations.B: This discussion informs management of the findings of the audit. Based on these discussions, management may agree to develop an implementation plan for the suggested recommendations, along with the timelines.
wrong_explanations.D: At the draft report stage, the IS auditor may recommend various controls to mitigate the risk, but the purpose of the meeting is to validate the findings of the audit with management.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: Which of the following responsibilities is MOST likely to compromise the independence of an information systems (IS) auditor when reviewing the risk management process?

options.A: Participating in the design of the risk management framework
options.B: Advising on different implementation techniques
options.C: Facilitating risk awareness training
options.D: Performing a due diligence review of the risk management processes

questions.correct_explanation: Participating in the design of the risk management framework involves designing controls, which compromises the independence of the information systems (IS) auditor to audit the risk management process.

wrong_explanations.B: Advising on different implementation techniques does not compromise the IS auditor's independence because the IS auditor will not be involved in the decision-making process.
wrong_explanations.C: Facilitating awareness training does not hamper the IS auditor's independence because the auditor will not be involved in the decision-making process.
wrong_explanations.D: Due diligence reviews are a type of audit generally related to mergers and acquisitions.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the GREATEST concern if audit objectives are not established during the initial phase of an audit program?

options.A: Key stakeholders are incorrectly identified.
options.B: Control costs will exceed the planned budget.
options.C: Important business risk may be overlooked.
options.D: Previously audited areas may be inadvertently included.

questions.correct_explanation: Without an audit scope, the appropriate risk assessment has not been performed, and therefore, the auditor might not audit those areas of highest risk for the organization.

wrong_explanations.A: In certain cases, it may be difficult to discuss findings when incorrect stakeholders are identified, thus delaying the communication of audit findings. However, this is not as concerning as important business risk not being included in audit scope.
wrong_explanations.B: Many factors determine the cost of controls. Therefore, it is difficult to state that only audit objectives will determine the control cost. However, this is not as important if the key risk is not identified.
wrong_explanations.D: Auditing previously audited areas is not an efficient use of resources; however, this is not as big of a concern as key risk not being identified.

tips: GREATEST risk/concern questions reward the option with the broadest blast radius, irreversibility, or regulatory exposure.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor wants to analyze audit trails on critical servers to discover potential anomalies in user or system behavior. Which of the following is the MOST suitable for performing that task?

options.A: Computer-aided software engineering tools
options.B: Embedded data collection tools
options.C: Trend/variance detection tools
options.D: Heuristic scanning tools

questions.correct_explanation: Trend/variance detection tools look for anomalies in user or system behavior, such as invoices with increasing invoice numbers.

wrong_explanations.A: Computer-aided software engineering tools are used to assist in software development.
wrong_explanations.B: Embedded (audit) data collection software, such as systems control audit review file or systems audit review file, is used to provide sampling and production statistics, but not to conduct an audit log analysis.
wrong_explanations.D: Heuristic scanning tools are a type of virus scanning used to indicate possible infected traffic.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: While performing an audit of an accounting application's internal data integrity controls, an information systems (IS) auditor identifies a major control deficiency in the change management software supporting the accounting application. The MOST appropriate action for the IS auditor to take is to:

options.A: continue to test the accounting application controls and inform the IT manager about the control deficiency and recommend possible solutions.
options.B: complete the audit and not report the control deficiency because it is not part of the audit scope.
options.C: continue to test the accounting application controls and include the deficiency in the final report.
options.D: cease all audit activity until the control deficiency is resolved.

questions.correct_explanation: It is the responsibility of the IS auditor to report on findings that can have a material impact on the effectiveness of controls-whether they are within the scope of the audit.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor should not assume that the IT manager will follow through on a verbal notification to resolve the change management control deficiency, and it is inappropriate to offer consulting services on issues discovered during an audit.
wrong_explanations.B: Although not technically within the audit scope, it is the responsibility of the IS auditor to report findings discovered during an audit that can have a material impact on the effectiveness of controls.
wrong_explanations.D: It is not the role of the IS auditor to demand that IT work be completed before performing or completing an audit.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: Which of the following will MOST successfully identify overlapping key controls in business application systems?

options.A: Reviewing system functionalities that are attached to complex business processes
options.B: Submitting test transactions through an integrated test facility
options.C: Replacing manual monitoring with an automated auditing solution
options.D: Testing controls to validate that they are effective

questions.correct_explanation: As part of the effort to realize continuous audit management, there are cases for introducing an automated monitoring and auditing solution. All key controls need to be clearly aligned for systematic implementation; thus, analysts can discover unnecessary or overlapping key controls in existing systems.

wrong_explanations.A: In general, highly complex business processes may have more key controls than business areas with less complexity; however, finding, with certainty, unnecessary controls in complex areas is not always possible. If a well-thought-out key control structure was established from the beginning, finding any overlap in key controls will not be possible.
wrong_explanations.B: An integrated test facility is an audit technique to test the accuracy of the processes in the application system. This technique may find control flaws in the application system, but it would be difficult for it to find the overlap in key controls.
wrong_explanations.D: By testing controls to validate whether they are effective, the information systems (IS) auditor can identify whether there are overlapping controls; however, the process of implementing an automated auditing solution better identifies overlapping controls.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: When performing a risk analysis, the information systems (IS) auditor should FIRST:

options.A: review the data classification program.
options.B: Identify the organization's information assets.
options.C: identify the inherent risk of the system.
options.D: perform a cost-benefit analysis for controls.

questions.correct_explanation: The first step of the risk assessment process is to identify the systems and processes that support the business objectives because risk to those processes impacts the achievement of business goals.

wrong_explanations.A: After the business objectives and the underlying systems are identified, the greatest degree of risk management effort should be focused on those assets containing data considered most sensitive to the organization. The data classification program assists the information systems (IS) auditor in identifying these assets.
wrong_explanations.C: Inherent risk is exposure without considering the actions that management has taken or might take. The purpose of a risk assessment is to identify vulnerabilities so that mitigating controls can be established. However, one must first understand the business and its supporting systems to best identify systems requiring the most risk assessment effort.
wrong_explanations.D: Designing and implementing controls to mitigate inherent risk of critical systems can only be performed after the above steps have been taken.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).

questions.question: After identifying the findings, the information systems (IS) auditor should FIRST:

options.A: gain agreement on the findings.
options.B: determine mitigation measures for the findings.
options.C: inform senior management of the findings.
options.D: obtain remediation deadlines to close the findings.

questions.correct_explanation: Iffindings are not agreed upon and confirmed by both parties, then there may be an issue during sign-off on the final audit report or while discussing findings with management. When an agreement is obtained with the auditee, it implies that the finding is understood and a clear plan of action can be determined.

wrong_explanations.B: Although the auditor may recommend mitigation measures, the organization ultimately decides and implements the mitigation strategies as a function of risk management.
wrong_explanations.C: Before senior management is informed, it is imperative that the auditor informs the auditee and gains agreement on the audit findings to correctly communicate the risk.
wrong_explanations.D: Obtaining remediation deadlines to close the findings is not the first step in communicating the audit findings.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).
When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: A PRIMARY benefit derived for an organization employing control self-assessment (CSA) techniques is that it:

options.A: can identify high-risk areas that might need a detailed review later.
options.B: allows information systems (IS) auditors to independently assess risk.
options.C: can be used as a replacement for traditional audits.
options.D: allows management to relinquish responsibility for control.

questions.correct_explanation: Control self-assessment (CSA) is predicated on the review of high-risk areas that either need immediate attention or may require a more thorough review later.

wrong_explanations.B: CSA requires the involvement of information systems (IS) auditors and line management. The internal audit function shifts some of the control monitoring responsibilities to the functional areas.
wrong_explanations.C: CSA is not a replacement for traditional audits. CSA is not intended to replace audit's responsibilities, but to enhance them.
wrong_explanations.D: CSA does not allow management to relinquish its responsibility for control.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: Which of the following is the FIRST step performed prior to creating a risk ranking for the annual internal information systems (IS) audit plan?

options.A: Prioritize the identified risk.
options.B: Define the audit universe.
options.C: Identify the critical controls.
options.D: Determine the testing approach.

questions.correct_explanation: In a risk-based audit approach, the IS auditor identifies risk to the organization based on the nature of the business. To plan an annual audit cycle, the types of risk must be ranked. To rank the types of risk, the auditor must first define the audit universe by considering the IT strategic plan, organizational structure and authorization matrix.

wrong_explanations.A: After the audit universe is defined, the information systems (IS) auditor can prioritize risk based on its overall impact on different operational areas of the organization covered under the audit universe.
wrong_explanations.C: The controls that help in mitigating high-risk areas are generally critical controls and their effectiveness provides assurance on mitigation of risk. However, this cannot be done unless the types of risk are ranked.
wrong_explanations.D: The testing approach is based on the risk ranking.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).
Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST likely to be considered a conflict of interest for an information systems (IS) auditor who is reviewing a cybersecurity implementation?

options.A: Delivering cybersecurity awareness training
options.B: Designing the cybersecurity controls
options.C: Advising on the cybersecurity framework
options.D: Conducting the vulnerability assessment

questions.correct_explanation: If an auditor designs the controls, a conflict of interest arises in the neutrality of the auditor to address deficiencies during an audit. This is in violation of the ISACA Code of Ethics.

wrong_explanations.A: Delivering cybersecurity awareness training is typically an operational responsibility, but it is not nearly as strong a conflict of interest as the auditor designing controls and then reviewing them.
wrong_explanations.C: Part of the role of an information systems (IS) auditor can be to advise on a cybersecurity framework, provided that such advice does not rise to the level of designing specific controls that the auditor would later review.
wrong_explanations.D: Conducting a vulnerability assessment can be the responsibility of the IS auditor and does not present a conflict of interest.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor identifies a business process to be audited. The IS auditor should NEXT identify the:

options.A: most valuable information assets.
options.B: IS audit resources to be deployed.
options.C: auditee personnel to be interviewed.
options.D: control objectives and activities.

questions.correct_explanation: After the business process is identified, the IS auditor should first identify the control objectives and activities associated with the business process that should be validated in the audit.

wrong_explanations.A: All assets need to be identified, not just information assets. To determine the key information assets to be audited, the information systems (IS) auditor should first determine which control objectives and key control activities should be validated. Only information assets that are related to the control objectives and key control activities are relevant for scoping the audit.
wrong_explanations.B: Only after determining which controls and related relevant information assets are to be validated can the IS auditor decide on the key IS audit resources (with the relevant skill sets) that should be deployed for the audit.
wrong_explanations.C: Only after determining the key control activities to be validated can the IS auditor identify the relevant process personnel who should be interviewed.

tips: Watch for separation-of-duties violations: the same actor authorizing AND executing, designing AND testing, or developing AND deploying.

questions.question: The effect of which of the following should have priority when planning the scope and objectives of an information systems (IS) audit?

options.A: Applicable statutory requirements
options.B: Applicable corporate standards
options.C: Applicable industry good practices
options.D: Organizational policies and procedures

questions.correct_explanation: The effect of applicable statutory requirements must be factored in while planning an information systems (IS) audit-the IS auditor has no options regarding statutory requirements because there can be no limitation of scope relating to statutory requirements.

wrong_explanations.B: Statutory requirements always take priority over corporate standards.
wrong_explanations.C: Industry good practices help plan an audit; however, good practices are not mandatory and can be deviated from, to meet organization objectives.
wrong_explanations.D: Organizational policies and procedures are important, but statutory requirements always take priority. Organizational policies must be in alignment with statutory requirements.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An external information systems (IS) auditor discovers that systems in the scope of the audit were implemented by an associate. In such a circumstance, IS audit management should:

options.A: remove the IS auditor from the engagement.
options.B: cancel the engagement.
options.C: disclose the issue to the client.
options.D: take steps to restore the IS auditor's independence.

questions.correct_explanation:
In circumstances in which the IS auditor's independence is impaired and the IS auditor continues 
to be associated with the audit, the facts surrounding the issue of the IS auditor's independence 
should be disclosed to the appropriate management and in the report.

wrong_explanations.A:
It is not necessary to withdraw the information systems (IS) auditor unless there is a statutory limitation, 
which exists in certain countries.
wrong_explanations.B: Canceling the engagement is not required if properly disclosed and accepted.
wrong_explanations.D:
This is not a feasible solution. The independence of the IS auditor cannot be restored while continuing to 
conduct the audit.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question:
An information systems (IS) auditor is planning to evaluate the control design effectiveness that is related 
to an automated billing process. Which of the following is the MOST effective approach for the auditor to 
adopt?

options.A: Interview
options.B: Inquiry
options.C: Reperformance
options.D: Walk-through

questions.correct_explanation: Reperformance is used to evaluate the operating effectiveness of the control rather than the design of the control.

wrong_explanations.A: An interview is not as strong evidence as an observation or walk-throughs. In addition, personnel might add some bias to interviews if they know they are being interviewed for an audit.
wrong_explanations.B: Inquiry can be used to understand the controls in a process only if it is accompanied by verification of evidence. However, interviewees might be biased if they know they are being audited.
wrong_explanations.D: Walk-throughs involve a combination of inquiry and inspection of evidence with respect to business process controls. This is the most effective basis for evaluation of the design of the control because it confirms that the control actually exists.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MAIN reason to perform a risk assessment in the planning phase of an information systems (IS) audit?

options.A: To ensure that management concerns are addressed
options.B: To provide reasonable assurance that material items will be addressed
options.C: To ensure that the audit team will perform audits within budget
options.D: To develop audit program and procedures needed to perform the audit

questions.correct_explanation: A risk assessment helps to focus the audit procedures on the highest risk areas included in the scope of the audit. The concept of reasonable assurance is also important.

wrong_explanations.A: Management concerns have no bearing on the risk assessment process. If management has concerns and wants the auditor to focus on a certain area, the auditor should ensure adequate time is allocated to address the concerns.
wrong_explanations.C: A risk assessment is performed to determine where to place time and personnel resources, while budget constraints are limited to time resources.
wrong_explanations.D: A risk assessment is not used in the development of the audit program and procedures. However, the risk assessment is used to allocate resources to audits.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST important to ensure before communicating the audit findings to top management during the closing meeting?

options.A: Risk statement includes an explanation of a business impact
options.B: Findings are clearly tracked back to evidence
options.C: Recommendations address root causes of findings
options.D: Remediation plans are provided by responsible parties

questions.correct_explanation: This will not necessarily reduce the time to have access to the information, because time will need to be scheduled for training and granting access.

wrong_explanations.A: Although the burden on human resources to support the audit may decrease if the information systems (IS) auditor directly extracts the data, this advantage is not as significant as the increased data validity.
wrong_explanations.C: There may be more flexibility for the IS auditor to adjust the data extracts to meet various audit requirements; however, this is not the main advantage.
wrong_explanations.D: If the IS auditor executes the data extraction, there is greater assurance that the extraction criteria will not interfere with the required completeness, and, therefore, all required data will be collected. Asking IT to extract the data may expose the risk of filtering out exceptions that should be seen by the auditor. Also, if the IS auditor collects the data, all internal references correlating the various data tables/elements will be understood, and this knowledge may reveal vital elements to the completeness and correctness of the overall audit activity.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
When in doubt about findings, document and report to management first — never act unilaterally to fix, escalate to regulators, or notify the audit committee prematurely.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor wants to determine the number of purchase orders that are not appropriately approved. Which of the following sampling techniques should an IS auditor use to make such a conclusion?

options.A: Attribute
options.B: Variable
options.C: Stop-or-go
options.D: Judgment

questions.correct_explanation: Attribute sampling is used to test compliance of transactions to controls-in this instance, the existence of appropriate approval.

wrong_explanations.B: Variable sampling is used in substantive testing situations and deals with population characteristics that vary, such as monetary values and weights.
wrong_explanations.C: Stop-or-go sampling is used when the expected occurrence rate is extremely low.
wrong_explanations.D: Judgment sampling is not relevant here. It refers to a subjective approach of determining sample size and selection criteria of elements of the sample.

tips: Compliance testing → attribute sampling. Substantive testing → variable sampling. Fraud screening → discovery sampling.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor uses computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs) to collect and analyze data. Which of the following attributes of evidence is MOST affected by using CAATs?

options.A: Usefulness
options.B: Reliability
options.C: Relevance
options.D: Adequacy

questions.correct_explanation: Because the data are directly collected by the information systems (IS) auditor, the audit findings can be reported with an emphasis on the reliability of the records that are produced and maintained in the system. The reliability of the source of information used provides reassurance on the generated findings.

wrong_explanations.A: Usefulness of audit evidence pulled by computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs) is determined by the audit objective, and the use of CAATs does not have as direct of an impact on usefulness as reliability.
wrong_explanations.C: Relevance of audit evidence pulled by CAATs is determined by the audit objective, and the use of CAATs does not have as direct of an impact on relevance as reliability.
wrong_explanations.D: Adequacy of audit evidence pulled by CAATs is determined by the processes and personnel who author the data, and the use of CAATs does not have any impact on competence.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Evidence reliability ranks: auditor-generated > independent third-party > internal system-generated > management assertion. Pick the most objective source.

questions.question: An internal information systems (IS) audit function is planning a general IS audit. Which of the following activities takes place during the FIRST step of the planning phase?

options.A: Developing an audit program
options.B: Defining the audit scope
options.C: Identifying key information owners
options.D: Developing a risk assessment

questions.correct_explanation: A risk assessment should be performed to determine how internal audit resources should be allocated to ensure that all material items will be addressed.

wrong_explanations.A: The results of the risk assessment are used for the input for the audit program.
wrong_explanations.B: The output of the risk assessment helps define the scope.
wrong_explanations.C: A risk assessment must be performed prior to identifying key information owners. Key information owners are generally not directly involved during the planning process of an audit.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).
Risk-based audit planning always starts with risk assessment — operational considerations (resources, schedule, management preference) come after.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST important skill that an information systems (IS) auditor should develop to understand the constraints of conducting an audit?

options.A: Managing audit staff
options.B: Allocating resources
options.C: Project management
options.D: Attention to detail

questions.correct_explanation: Audits often involve resource management, deliverables, scheduling and deadlines that are similar to project management good practices.

wrong_explanations.A: Managing audit staff is not the only aspect of conducting an audit.
wrong_explanations.B: Allocating resources, such as time and personnel, is needed for overall project management skills.
wrong_explanations.D: Attention to detail is needed, but it is not a constraint of conducting audits.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: What is the MAJOR benefit of conducting a control self-assessment (CSA) over a traditional audit?

options.A: It detects risk sooner.
options.B: It replaces the internal audit function.
options.C: It reduces the audit workload.
options.D: It reduces audit resource requirements.

questions.correct_explanation: Control self-assessments (CSAs) require employees to assess the control stature of their own function. CSAs help to increase the understanding of business risk and internal controls. Because they are conducted more frequently than audits, CSAs help to identify risk in a timelier manner.

wrong_explanations.B: CSAs do not replace the internal audit function; an audit must still be performed to ensure that controls are present.
wrong_explanations.C: CSAs may not reduce the audit function's workload and are not a major difference between the two approaches.
